question: On 5 October 2026, in a world first, a National Institutes of Health (NIH) clinic dedicated to vaccine victims opened in Bethesda, Maryland. In future, doctors are also to be remunerated for reporting suspected vaccine side-effects in the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS).

At the clinic, doctors and scientists are to examine patients, document the course of their illness, investigate possible causes and devise better approaches to their care. It is high time that vaccine injuries were taken seriously and vaccines made safer. Unsafe vaccines need to be pulled from the market with immediate effect.

After all, the figures paint a clear picture: the number of COVID-vaccine-associated injuries entered in the reporting systems managed by the EU, the US and the WHO is several times higher than for all other vaccines combined. 1.

Why has the Commission shown zero interest to date in meticulously identifying, documenting, investigating and treating possible vaccine injuries, despite the responsibility it carries for having negotiated and signed deals with pharmaceutical companies to procure the COVID-19 vaccines without sufficient evidence and testing?
Why does it not also fund such a clinic?

Why does the Commission not follow in the footsteps of the US and step up the work of the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control and improve the European Medicines Agency’s database of suspected side-effects?
